title: Nf Maxorder Om Deep
objective: Extend certified OM/MaxMin beyond first-order linear residue keys to a bounded higher-representative and residual-extension domain with differential basis/index evidence

handoff.summary: Extends the strict-Python OM/MaxMin lane with bounded finite residual fields F_(p^m), deterministic residual factorization, inspectable same-degree representative refinement, active-versus-optimized local-index evidence, quotient tables for nonlinear keys, and real multi-branch MaxMin. CPython and Sage.js certify identical bases through degree 16 and local index valuation 120; an offline Sage 10.9/PARI-family run proves exact maximal-order lattice equality for every completed fixture.
risks: Degree-raising higher representatives remain explicitly incomplete; the fixture x^4 + 4*x + 4 retains requires-degree-raising-representative rather than claiming completeness.
Residual factorization is deliberately exhaustive and bounded at 200000 candidates; larger residue fields need the planned FLINT fq/fq_nmod path.
Dynamic Sage.js remains 50-630 ms on the measured corpus, so automatic selector evidence stays disabled pending source-transparent/native polynomial loops.

The base c31f545b native suite has an unrelated nine-symbol FLINT FFI ratchet mismatch for the newly integrated number-field-order resource and stale production-kernel metadata; pnpm test:native therefore cannot be a clean lane receipt.
next_steps: Implement degree-raising MacLane valuations and higher residual operators, retaining the current fail-closed state until independently certified.
Replace bounded residual enumeration with declared FLINT fq/fq_nmod operations after measuring the crossover.
Source-transparently compile polynomial/residual loops before considering OM auto-selection.
Rerun native and Windows/arm64 matrices after the integration lane repairs the c31f545b FFI ratchets.
